literal: To those who punished, one day's pleasure; to those who forbore, until-perishing glory.
translation: Those who punish an offense find pleasure for a single day, but those who bear it patiently gain glory that lasts until the end of time.
modern: பிறர் செய்த தவற்றைத் தண்டிப்பவருக்கு அந்த ஒரு நாள் மட்டுமே இன்பம் கிடைக்கும். ஆனால் அதனைப் பொறுத்துக்கொள்பவருக்கு உலகம் அழியும் வரை புகழ் நிலைத்திருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the fleeting satisfaction of retaliation with the enduring legacy of forgiveness. The phrase 'oru nāḷai iṉpam' highlights that punishing an offender offers only a brief, single day of emotional release. In contrast, 'poṉṟum tuṇaiyum pukaḻ' reveals that choosing to patiently bear an offense earns a person glory that lasts until the very end of time. By juxtaposing these two outcomes, the poet emphasizes that true greatness lies in forbearance rather than revenge.
